text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
CHARLES BOWEN, a controversial Anglican in early Australia, was born in 1803. His publications led him to be thrown out of the Church of England.
Sir CHARLES HOTHAM was born in England in 1806, and was Governor of Victoria during the EUREKA STOCKADE REBELLION.
Sir WILLIAM ROBINSON was born in Ireland in 1834, and became Governor of South Australia, as well as a popular songwriter.
JULES FRANCOIS ARCHIBALD was born in 1856, and is remembered for his art prize, as well as the major fountain in Sydney's HYDE PARK. He owned the BULLETIN MAGAZINE.
The French missionary and philosopher ALBERT SCHWIETZER was born on this day in 1875. He won the NOBEL PEACE PRIZE in 1952.

Australian Naval Officer ROWLAND BOWEN was born in 1879. In 1914 he captured a German patrol in New Guinea, by falsely claiming that 800 Australian troops were advancing on the area! The German Governor believed him, and abandoned the colony.
British stage designer and photographer CECIL BEATON was born in 1904.

US singer who first appeared professionally at the age of 13, BILLIE JO SPEARS, was born in 1937. She was very successful in country charts from 1968 to 1984. Hits included "Mr Walker It's All Over" (1969), "Blanket On The Ground" (1975) and "What I've Got In Mind" (1976). In the United Kingdom she replaced TAMMY WYNETTE as the best selling country artist.
The popular American singer JACK JONES was born on this day in 1938.
American actress FAYE DUNAWAY was born in 1941. Her movie successes included "BONNIE AND CLYDE" and "THE THOMAS CROWN AFFAIR".

United States rapper and rap writer L.L.COOL J. (JAMES TODD SMITH) was born in 1968. He had his first major hits in late 1985 on the R & B charts. His 1987 single "I Need Love" brought him wider popularity.
** EVENTS **
1742 : Sir EDMUND HALLEY, the British astronomer who gave
his name to the famous comet, died.
1753 : Philosopher and Bishop GEORGE BERKELEY died. He
was one of the most influential thinkers of his time, supporting the idealistic claim - "If you don't think about it, it's not there!"
1815 : A big day in the history of NSW - the road over
the Blue Mountains to Bathurst was completed, after six-months of development
1878 : Queen Victoria was given a demonstration of the
new device invented by ALEXANDER GRAHAM BELL - the telephone.
1898 : The creator of "ALICE IN WONDERLAND", LEWIS
CARROLL (Charles Dodgson), died at the age of 66.
1900 : Puccini's opera "Tosca" first staged in Rome.
1907 : A massive earthquake destroyed most of the
Jamaican capital Kingston, killing more than a thousand people.
1938 : "SNOW WHITE AND THE SEVEN DWARFS", the first Walt
Disney full-length Technicolour cartoon, went on general release in the United States.
1954 : MARILYN MONROE (Norma Jean Baker), who'd starred
in "HOW TO MARRY A MILLIONAIRE", did just that by wedding baseball-hero JOE DIMAGGIO.
1957 : HUMPHREY BOGART, the enormously popular Hollywood
star, died.
1977 : Australian actor PETER FINCH died at the age of

60. He was said to be at the height of his fame having just starred in the movie "Network" as a crazed television newsreader. Some critics regarded this performance as the high spot of his career. Australians remembered him for his 1956 role in the film "A Town Like Alice". His career began when at the age of 21 he played "Dave" in the 1938 comedy film "Dad and Dave Come To Town".
1982 : The son of British Prime Minister MARGARET
THATCHER, MARK, was found in the Sahara Desert after disappearing during the Paris/Dakar motor rally.
1984 : The founder of the McDONALD's empire, RAY KROC,

died. It's estimated there are close to 8-thousand McDONALD's restaurants in 32 countries around the world, turning over more than 10 billion dollars in annual sales. Mr KROC claimed to have made more people into millionaires, through franchising, than anyone else in history!
1986 : The VOYAGER 2 spacecraft passed within 80,000 km
of the planet URANUS, after collecting data on the planet for several months.
1989 : British Muslims staged a demonstration, burning
copies of the controversial SALMAN RUSHDIE book "THE SATANIC VERSES".
1990 : 43 people died as fire swept through a popular
nightclub in Saragossa, Spain.
1995 : The British Army ended 25 years of daylight
patrols in Belfast in a wind-down of a guerrilla conflict which engulfed Northern Ireland.
